scoring.surface: POST /context/prompt, fresh session per case, whole injected block (spores and plans)
scoring.positive: every expected id served and no mustNot id served
scoring.negative: nothing injected at all (no spore, no plan)
scoring.plans: no plan is expected in any case; every served plan counts as unwanted
scoring.ratchet: per case and target: no expected id served at baseline may drop; no unwanted id absent at baseline may appear; pass count may not drop

cases.why: Bun SQLite has no setAuthorizer; use prepared statements to parse trigger bodies. MP saturates (0.92–0.999 for all six), so the band admits everything; SCHEMA_STEPS and RelationalStore.batch are adjacent, the cross-lane-hunk pattern and self-hosted update are not.
cases.prompt: Parent checked the local bun-types SQLite API: no public setAuthorizer API. Avoid FFI/native internals for this bounded slice. A useful verified primitive: db.prepare("CREATE TABLE one(x); CREATE TABLE two(y)").run() creates only one, not two. A prepared statement lets SQLite own trigger-body parsing while schema equality can reject trailing schema garbage; it avoids db.exec multi-statement side effects in schema.json. The existing splitter already isolates ordinary dump statements, so constrain allowed statement forms there rather than adding another parser. Retain tests for comments/literals, NUL rewrite and required sqlite_sequence/PRAGMA handling. For schema entries, validate the declared kind/storage and actual CREATE statement kind, then prepare/run one statement; prove injected ATTACH/UPDATE tail cannot execute. This is guidance from local verification, not a mandated implementation if you find a smaller safe existing pattern.

cases.why: Retention default stays keep-forever. The '2.0 retention: keep 1.4's guards' gotcha is right and the capture-volume decision adjacent; backup, embedding receipts and writeOrigin are noise.
cases.prompt:
Correction from the product owner on the retention addition: the DEFAULT stays keep-forever (unset). Don't add a 90-day default. Retention stays configurable through `retention.transcripts` as it is today. Keep the rest of the addition:
(b) `myco stats` shows the retention window next to the storage facts, e.g. "Transcripts: raw bytes kept forever (no retention set)" or "kept N days after processing".
(c) The ledger records the decision: capture is never refused for volume; storage is managed by the owner-configurable retention of processed raw transcript bytes (default keep forever).
(d) Tests: unset means nothing is pruned; with N days set, a processed segment older than N is pruned, an unprocessed one is kept, and derived rows survive.
Make sure the Settings description of `retention.transcripts` says plainly what it prunes (processed raw transcript bytes only; everything derived is kept) and that unset means keep forever.
